snippet.title: Why Delhi has almost no skyscrapers #Shorts
snippet.description:
Gurgaon and Noida are full of towers, yet Delhi stayed low for three reasons: airport height clearances, 174 protected monuments, and the low-rise Lutyens' bungalow zone. Then in August 2026 the Master Plan for Delhi 2047 removed height limits across most of the city.

Would you live on the 50th floor in Delhi?

Sources: Height Restriction Rules 2015 (GSR 751(E)); ASI / AMASR Act; CTBUH; MPD 2047 (Aug 2026).
Some visuals are AI generated. Educational content, not investment advice.

snippet.title: Why the Supreme Court ordered Noida's twin towers blown up #Shorts
snippet.description:
Two towers taller than Qutub Minar, never lived in, brought down in seconds on 28 Aug 2022. The case: a revised plan put them on land shown to buyers as green area, the gap to an existing tower was about 9 m against a required 16 m, and residents were never asked for consent. The Supreme Court upheld demolition in Aug 2021 and ordered refunds with 12% interest.

Right call, or a waste?

Sources: Supreme Court of India, Supertech Ltd v. Emerald Court Owner RWA (31 Aug 2021); Allahabad High Court (Apr 2014).
Visuals are AI visualisations, not the real site. Educational content, not legal or investment advice.
